summary:
Build attempt 3 (bb3b011) touched two files; the product source is unchanged (SynchronousIoCancel.cs is still C4E31B83…).

**Rule 2 in .taad/fitness.yaml (O-028).**
- The ThreadPool pattern now exempts only Close's `ThreadPool.UnsafeQueueUserWorkItem(static aborted =>`, and `\bnew\s+Task\s*[(<]` was added. The `because` names the one exempt call site.
- I read the patterns back from the YAML and ran them with Python `re`, the engine's dialect.
  - The current file gets 0 hits.
  - A pool-queued attempt (`static g => g.CancelOnce()`) is caught by the ThreadPool pattern.
  - `new Task(CancelOnce).Start()` is caught by the new pattern.
  - A fully qualified Close still passes.
  - Reformatting Close's call (a line break or a space after `UnsafeQueueUserWorkItem`) fires the rule on legitimate code. That fails loudly, not silently, so I noted it as drift rather than a finding.
  - Only a pool attempt whose lambda parameter is also named `aborted` evades the rule, which is contrived.
- The Fitness engine re-parsed all 52 rules and every one holds, and rules-parity says AGREE.

**CancelIsResentUntilACallThatHadNotReachedTheKernelIsInterrupted.**
- The fixed 200 ms sleep is gone. The worker now waits until `CancelAttempts >= 2` (up to 5 s), then 100 ms more, before it blocks, and asserts that those attempts were sent. The Join is raised to 10 s.
- `CancelAttempts` counts attempts that passed the gate, not calls made. The 100 ms makes that gap irrelevant, and the assertion only needs one miss.
- I ran three mutants in a temp copy, since deleted:
  - A canceller that stops resending once it gets FALSE/1168: red 2 of 2 ('the wait was never interrupted'). This is the shape design case C-004 says would bring back the lost cancel.
  - A canceller with no resend: red 2 of 2.
  - Every attempt delayed 300 ms: green 2 of 2, so the test no longer depends on how fast the first attempt arrives.
- No other test depends on the first attempt arriving within a fixed sleep; I grepped every `Cancel();` site in tests/.

**What I ran on the current tree.**
- Build: 0 warnings, 0 errors.
- Acceptance command: exit 0, 2 of 2 passed.
- Both guard classes, 5 idle runs: 30 of 30 each.
- Full suite: 337 of 337.
- Concentrated loaded pass (4 busy processes and the test host pinned to CPUs 14–15): 3 of 3 runs, 30 of 30 each. The reworked test took 0.87–0.93 s. Afterwards no busy loops or testhosts were left.

The working tree is as I found it: only the engine's index.json and build-slice-3.json differ.

Second round: Round 2 found nothing to file.

**Rule 2 regexes, probed with Python `re` on patterns read back from the YAML.** The attempt-3 patterns catch the forms they target. Four other forms still slip past:
- `ThreadPool` + newline + `.UnsafeQueueUserWorkItem(static g => …)`
- `Task.Factory` + newline + `.StartNew(`
- `using static System.Threading.ThreadPool` followed by a bare `UnsafeQueueUserWorkItem(`
- `Task.Run<int>(`

The last two are the same slips my attempt-1 review accepted for a name tripwire. The first two are new instances of that same family. This is the second time a rule-2 evasion has come up after R2-m1, and a regex can always be dodged one step further out. So I recorded it as drift with the approach-level fix: a behavioural check that no attempt runs on a pool thread. I did not send it back again.

**fitness.yaml.** It still has no BOM, 678 CRLF line endings, no bare LF, no lone CR and no tabs. The multi-line plain `because` is valid YAML, and the engine parses all 52 rules. No rule-harness plant row or parity entry names rule 2, so changing its patterns shifts no count.

**The reworked C-004 test (SynchronousIoCancelTests.cs:66-109).**
- The worker spins with `SpinWait.SpinUntil`, which yields and sleeps, so it does not starve the canceller or the attempt threads.
- Early attempts land on a non-I/O wait and get FALSE.
- The 100 ms margin covers the gap between an attempt passing the gate and it actually calling CancelSynchronousIo.
- The failure path of a canceller that never resends leaves a background thread blocked on a pipe that is disposed. The old version of this test had the same failure path; it is not new here.
- My round-1 mutants still stand: terminal-on-FALSE and no-resend go red, and the 300 ms late-attempt mutant stays green.

Both changed files keep consistent CRLF line endings. The working tree is as I found it.

obligations.evidence: I ran the acceptance command on the current tree: exit 0, 2 of 2 passed.
Both repro tests (one CPU, worker at Highest, 3 and 8 waits) are green idle and in 3 of 3 loaded runs. Each attempt runs on its own thread (SynchronousIoCancel.cs:359-408, unchanged).
The unbounded drain (SynchronousIoCancel.cs:422-431) never hung in 5 idle class runs, the full suite or 3 loaded runs, all with blame-hang 60 s. Proven for local pipes only.

The post-Exit pending pipe wait is still in the repro (lines 108-112) and in ExitWaits (SynchronousIoCancelTests.cs:241-246). It went red against the no-wait Drain mutant in my attempt-2 run; src is unchanged since.
The working premise holds: the repro, red before the fix, is green.
The drain is still unbounded, there is no bounded drain, the handle is still a SafeThreadHandle, and the ObjectDisposedException catch is kept (SynchronousIoCancel.cs:60, 399-403, 419-431).
C-001: CancelFreesACallThatBlocksAgainBeforeTheCancelCallHasReturned passes.
C-002: CancelIsResentWhileACallBlocksAgainAfterACancel is unchanged with its 2 s bar and was green in 3 of 3 concentrated loaded runs.
C-003: CancelInterruptsACallBlockedInTheKernel passes idle and loaded. Its first attempt always goes through a thread start.

C-004: the reworked test (SynchronousIoCancelTests.cs:66-109) still asserts attempts > delivered and a delivered resend. It is red on the terminal-on-FALSE and no-resend mutants and green on the 300 ms late-attempt mutant.
C-005: ExitWithNoCancelMakesNoAttemptAndWaitsForNone is unchanged and passes.
C-006: ExitWaits asserts liveAtExit >= 2 and the repro asserts >= 1. Both pass.
C-007: the post-Exit listing and pending wait are unchanged in both files.
C-008: DisposeWithoutExitWhileCancellingEndsEveryAttemptFirst is unchanged since attempt 2, where both Dispose mutants made it red.
C-009: the repro is in the ResendRace DisableParallelization collection with affinity restored. Full suite 337 of 337.
M1: `~SynchronousIoCancel` ran 30 tests covering both classes, idle and loaded.
M2: the post-Exit witness is a pending WaitForConnection with its client at 300 ms (SynchronousIoCancelTests.cs AssertNoCancelLandsOnThisThread).
M3: the 8-wait repro with a 10 s bar and the peak printed is unchanged (SynchronousIoCancelResendRaceTests.cs:53-55, 122-123).

M4: the _disposed and state checks under _gate (SynchronousIoCancel.cs:363, 390) and the Dispose ordering (265-282) are unchanged. The no-growth-after-Dispose assertion is at SynchronousIoCancelTests.cs:337-338.
Critique m1: the slot is reserved under _gate before Start, and released in the catch and in the finally (SynchronousIoCancel.cs:361-376, 404-407).
Critique m3: the rule exempts the Close hand-off and adds the Task.Factory, System.Timers and PeriodicTimer patterns. It is now narrowed further by O-028. Fitness: all 52 rules hold.
m4: the drain comment at SynchronousIoCancel.cs:419-421 records that there is no watchdog. Every loop I ran used blame-hang.
m5: Kernel32.cs:94-99 and SynchronousIoCancel.cs:23-27 describe the behaviour as observed on Windows 11 26200, against the documented Remarks.
m6 is a measurement report (loaded and idle full-suite runs reported apart), not code. Nothing in the tree can show it, and validate lists the concentrated full-suite run as not reached.
m7: there is one SL-055 rule in fitness.yaml, with a comment explaining why the SL-024 duplicate was dropped.
The Dispose test with held attempts and its three assertions (SynchronousIoCancelTests.cs:287-295, 333-335) is unchanged since my attempt-2 mutant runs, where it went red.
Assert.Equal(4, PeakAttemptsInKernel) at SynchronousIoCancelTests.cs:258 is unchanged. It was red with cap 5 in attempt 2.

cases.evidence: The repro pins the process to its lowest CPU, runs the worker at Highest and re-blocks 3 times. Red before the fix, green now.
CancelIsResentWhileACallBlocksAgainAfterACancel feeds 3 re-blocks. Load was concentrated on 2 CPUs, not the design's 32 jobs on 16 CPUs (validate's recorded gap).
Single pipe wait. The first attempt always goes through a new `scan-cancel-attempt` thread.

The reworked test keeps the worker in managed code until 2 attempts have passed the gate, plus 100 ms, so the early attempts return FALSE/1168. It then blocks and needs a resend. Red when FALSE ends the resend and when there is no resend at all; green with 300 ms attempt latency.
The token is never cancelled. Asserts attempts, peak and live-at-drain are all 0.
ExitWaits holds attempts 2 to 4 across Exit and asserts liveAtExit >= 2.
After Exit, a listing and then a pending 300 ms pipe wait, in the repro and in ExitWaits.
The Dispose test throws through the using with attempts held past the throw. Unchanged since the mutants that turned it red.
Serialized collection with affinity restored and asserted. Full suite 337 of 337 with the repro included.
ExitWaits drives the attempts to the cap and asserts Peak == 4.
Non-material and deliberately untested. The reason still holds: the spike measured 500 of 500 under 622 ms, and a latency assert would flake. Recorded at SynchronousIoCancel.cs:39-44.
Non-material; there is no seam to make Thread.Start throw. The catch calls EndAttempt (SynchronousIoCancel.cs:373-376) and CancelOnce never runs after a failed Start.

drift: Nothing undeclared departed. The reworked C-004 test (wait for 2 attempts plus 100 ms instead of a fixed 200 ms sleep) is declared, and the design's case C-004 is unchanged.

Rule 2's exemption now depends on how Close's call is written. A reformat that puts a line break or a space between `UnsafeQueueUserWorkItem` and `(static aborted` makes the rule fire on legitimate code (checked with Python re). It fails loudly and the `because` explains why, but whoever edits Close must keep that call on one line.

SL-049's opt-in CloudPlaceholderTests stall Fact is still the only test that would run SL-055's unbounded drain against a real redirector (cldflt). Its 5 s bar was justified on the pre-SL-055 guard, and it has not run on the new guard, because registering a sync root is still SL-049's open question for a person.
Nothing undeclared departed. The reworked C-004 test is a declared departure, and the design's case C-004 is unchanged.

Rule 2 is a name tripwire, and after O-028 it still has ways around it. Python `re` against the current patterns shows a pool-queued attempt written as `ThreadPool` + newline + `.UnsafeQueueUserWorkItem(static g => …)`, `Task.Factory` + newline + `.StartNew(`, `using static System.Threading.ThreadPool` with a bare `UnsafeQueueUserWorkItem(`, or `Task.Run<int>(` all pass. The same patterns fail on legitimate code if Close's call is wrapped after `(`. This is the second instance of this family after R2-m1, and a regex can always be dodged one step further out, so it is noted here rather than sent back. Two fixes, for whoever picks it up. First, the approach-level one: in an existing guard test, record `Thread.CurrentThread.IsThreadPoolThread` inside BeforeCancelCall and assert it is false. That catches every form, because the pool-queued mutant from round 2 of attempt 2 passed all 70 guard tests. Second, the smaller regex-only one: replace pattern 1 with `\bUnsafeQueueUserWorkItem\s*\((?!\s*static\s+aborted\b)` plus `\bThreadPool\s*\.\s*(?!UnsafeQueueUserWorkItem\b)`. The lookahead must include the `\s*`; a bare `\(\s*(?!…)` backtracks and still fires on a wrapped Close.

SL-049's opt-in CloudPlaceholderTests stall Fact is still the only test that would run SL-055's unbounded drain against a real redirector (cldflt). It has not been run on the new guard, because registering a sync root is still SL-049's open question for a person.
